Hi Emily — thanks for the clear list. Quick responses inline below; Marissa and Finance will share the official numbers and a PDF quote.

- Pricing model: high-level: monthly-billed reserved capacity is available (pay-as-you-go for reserved pool capacity billed monthly) and annual prepay gives you a significant term discount — typical starting point is ~12–20% vs monthly depending on commit and pool size. Exact tiering depends on GPU count and term.

- True-ups: we typically do usage metering daily and reconcile quarterly. For annual prepaid customers we do a quarterly true-up: if you exceed the committed throughput we invoice overage at the agreed overage rate; if you underuse we can (1) apply credits against future usage or (2) adjust the next term during renewal (not a cash refund). We can include auto-scale and burst capacity options.

- PO & invoicing: Redwood accepts customer POs. For annual prepay we issue an invoice upon contract signature (or per milestone if requested). Net30 is standard for customers with approved credit; Net45 is possible with procurement approval.

- Contracting: MSA + SOW is our standard. DocuSign is fine. We'll include an SLA statement for throughput and an appendix with measurement methodology.

I've looped in Marissa (pricing) and Monica (CS for SOW details) — they'll attach a formal quote and recommended sizing.

Thanks —

Emily / team — attaching a short proposal and an SOW workbook (stubs) for your packet. Highlights below: 

1) Recommended pool sizing & throughput SLA
- Recommendation: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved pool) to meet target 99th percentile latency < 250ms at peak of 120 concurrent streams. This includes configured KV cache and a 10% buffer for burst capacity.
- Throughput guarantee: 120 sustained concurrent streams with average token throughput 30 TPS, with automated fallback to a compatible model variant when capacity is constrained. SLO credit: service credit tiers scale if monthly P95 latency exceeds agreed threshold.

2) Pricing summary (illustrative)
- Monthly reserved billing: base rate $X per GPU / month (billed monthly). No upfront required.
- Annual prepay: 12-month prepay at invoice, 15% discount off list for the recommended 8 GPU commit. 24-month prepay available with 22% discount.
- Large-commit volume bands: additional 3–5% off for >16 GPU committed pools.

3) True-up mechanics
- Measurement: daily usage metrics, reconciled quarterly.
- Overage: usage above committed capacity billed at the overage rate (per GPU-hour).
- Underuse: for annual prepay, underuse is addressed via credit against future term or adjusted at renewal; we do not issue retroactive cash refunds.

4) Billing & procurement flow
- We accept customer POs and can invoice per your desired cadence (monthly for month-to-month reserved, annual invoice for prepay). Standard payment terms: Net30 after invoice.
- For annual prepay invoiced at signature, provide PO number and remit per invoice instructions.

5) Next steps

Hi Emily / Procurement team — finance here. Quick note to make the PO/invoice flow explicit so your accounting can process this quickly: 

- PO acceptance: Redwood accepts POs that reference the agreed quote number and include the billing address and tax ID. Please send PO to billing@redwood.com and cc your Redwood AE (ava_chen@redwood.com).

- Invoicing cadence:
  * Monthly reserved: invoice generated at the end of each calendar month for the preceding month (Net30).
  * Annual prepay: single invoice issued upon execution of the contract (Net30). If you prefer split invoicing (e.g., 50/50 at signature / 6 months) we can accommodate on a case-by-case basis; note this may impact discount eligibility.

- True-ups & overage handling: we meter usage continuously and run a quarterly reconciliation process. Overages are invoiced on the next monthly invoice after the reconciliation window. For annual prepay customers, overages are invoiced net30; underuse is applied as a credit to the next term (per the SOW).

- Payment methods: ACH (preferred), wire transfer, or corporate card for monthly invoices. Wires should reference the invoice number.

- Net terms & credit: Net30 is standard. If ScaleArc is requesting Net45 or extended terms, we need an approved credit application (we can fast-track this for strategic commitments).

- Contract & signature: we use DocuSign for MSA+SOW. Link to contract draft (view-only): https://app.redwood.example/docusign/12345. Once executed, finance will issue the annual invoice if you choose prepay.

Happy to hop on a short call with your AP team if that helps unblock the PO.

Best,
